content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — node gpu-n12 in us-west-2 reporting ephemeral storage usage > 94% and repeated pod restarts for modelcache pods. Triggers: eviction events + CUDA init failures. Auto-page P1.

oncall-alex: I'm up. Seeing a short burst of 503s on /v1/generate for a subset of requests. Triage - is this widespread or confined to dedicated hosts?

sre-maya: Looks localized to a handful of nodes in the us-west GPU pool. kubectl shows multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff / Evicted.

runtime-jordan: here's recent kubectl output (trimmed):
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep modelcache
modelcache-5f7bd9 1/1 Running 0 2m gpu-n12
modelcache-6c8a21 0/1 Evicted 0 1m gpu-n12
modelcache-9a3f00 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 3 30s gpu-n13
```

runtime-jordan: describe on the evicted pod: 
```
Reason: Evicted
Message: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage. Container cannot be scheduled.
Last State: Terminated
Exit Code: 1
```

eng-infra-lee: can you paste df/du from gpu-n12? I want to see what's filling /var/lib/kubelet/pods/modelcache...

runtime-jordan: attaching ssh output (sanitized):
```
$ ssh gpu-n12
# df -h /var/lib/kubelet
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p1  900G  825G   50G  95% /var/lib/kubelet

$ sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/pods/* | sort -h | tail -n 8
1.2G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<podid>/volumes
4.5G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<podid>/containers/modelcache
28G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<podid>/logs
72G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<podid2>/model-cache
```

oncall-alex: logs look like massive rotated logs + model cache spill files. Did a job start preloading a larger model?

runtime-jordan: We recently rolled a model variant that keeps a local disk-backed index for faster cold-starts. The cache eviction wasn't limiting size; config mismatch allowed unbounded growth.

eng-infra-lee: ack. Immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon and drain gpu-n12 to force pods to move, 2) delete large log files / restart kubelet to reclaim, 3) scale down modelcache replicas to reduce churn, 4) push a hotfix to enforce max-cache-size. Which do we do now?

oncall-alex: Prioritize low-risk quick wins: cordon + drain, rotate/delete logs on node, scale down modelcache to 1, and enable node-level eviction patch to drop pods holding large on-disk caches. Jordan — can you scale deployment?

runtime-jordan: scaling down modelcache to 1 now: `kubectl scale deploy/modelcache -n inference --replicas=1`

support-ash: Noted increased error volume. CS: Sam — heads up, some enterprise Dedicated customers may have seen 502/503s for a minute or two. I'm drafting a status update.

cs-lead-sam: Thanks. Which tenants are affected? Any high-severity SLAs hit?

support-ash: Preliminary: traffic spikes hit a small set of tenants pinned to us-west dedicated capacity. I'm pulling logs to map tenant IDs. Will attach list in 10m.

eng-infra-lee: cordoning node gpu-n12 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-n12`

oncall-alex: draining but keep eviction grace short: `kubectl drain gpu-n12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30`

incident-bot: Runbook step: if node ephemeral > 90% and eviction rate > 3 in 5m, cordon & drain.

runtime-jordan: drain started. Some pods failed to reschedule due to lack of capacity in the pool — we're seeing GPU pressure. I'll prioritize moving non-essential workloads off the pool.

eng-infra-lee: while we free up capacity, delete rotated logs older than 7 days from the problematic pods to reclaim space. Command: `find /var/lib/kubelet/pods -name "*.log" -mtime +7 -exec rm -f {} \;`

oncall-alex: Jordan please run targeted safe deletions only — don't remove anything the runtime expects. Use `du` to confirm files > 1G first.

runtime-jordan: running `du` and removing old logs now. reclaim ~60G so far.

sre-maya: I see kubelet evictions decreased after log removals. However we still have CUDA init failures on one host: `/var/log/syslog` contains `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus`. That indicates potential hardware glitch coinciding with disk pressure. Let's isolate that host.

eng-infra-lee: marking gpu-n13 as unschedulable for GPUs: `kubectl label node gpu-n13 problem=isolated` and opening infra ticket to investigate hardware.

runtime-jordan: applied max-cache-size env var override to deployment (hotfix): `MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=25000000000` and triggering rolling restart for remaining modelcache pods.

oncall-alex: good. Watch for restart storms. Set rollout pause if errors spike.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (auto). Severity P1. Link: https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-042

support-ash: Draft status update to customers: "We detected transient errors for requests routed to some GPU hosts in us-west. Root cause: node ephemeral storage saturation causing pod evictions and subsequent runtime restarts. We mitigated by cordoning/draining nodes, reclaiming disk, and applying a hotfix to limit local model cache size. Services have recovered; we’re monitoring."

cs-lead-sam: LGTM. Push to status page and include list of impacted tenants when available.

pm-oliver: Can we add a one-liner for external customers about expected latency window? e.g., "impacts between 14:22-14:25 UTC"

support-ash: putting time window in: 14:21–14:28 UTC.

sre-maya: Monitoring: tailing pod restarts + OOMs. Setting an alert to email if restart rate > 5/min for next 30m.

eng-infra-lee: follow-up items (backlog): enforce disk quota on modelcache volumes, add model-cache-size validation on rollout, integrate logrotation in pod init, and add a node-level cron to clear orphaned tmp files. I'll create GH issues.

runtime-jordan: quick note — observed one of the modelcache pods writing checkpoint files into `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../model-cache/checkpoints` without gc. Hotfix prevented new growth but we need GC logic in code.

oncall-alex: summary for handoff -> @sre-maya:
- Root cause: unbounded on-disk model cache + log growth led to ephemeral storage pressure -> kubelet evictions + pod restarts; concurrently a GPU host showed transient hardware GPU errors.
- Actions taken: cordoned/drained gpu-n12, isolated gpu-n13, rotated/removed old logs (~60G reclaimed), scaled modelcache to 1, applied MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES, rolling restarts.
- Customer impact: several dedicated-tenants in us-west saw 502/503 for ~1-2m; support has list (support-ash). Status page updated.

sre-maya: taking over monitoring. I'll watch restarts, eviction metrics, and error budgets for next 60m. If restart spike returns, we'll rollback the model variant.

support-ash: uploaded tenant list to INC-2026-042 and pinged CSMs.

pm-oliver: please add retrospective seat to calendar and include runtime + infra + product owners. Need to decide permanent limits and rollout gating.

sre-maya: acknowledged. Handoff notes saved to incident ticket. Thanks all.

oncall-alex: closing active page for now, will remain reachable if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

sre-maya: I'll post a postmortem draft in 24h; early blameless notes: config default allowed unbounded cache and logs weren't rotated for large payloads.

pm-oliver: thanks team.
